claims: NASA launched the Artemis II mission on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Artemis II marks the first crewed lunar flyby in over 50 years.
Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II is a 10-day mission.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket successfully lifted off from Launch Pad 39B.
Reid Wiseman is a NASA astronaut on Artemis II.
Victor Glover is a NASA astronaut on Artemis II.
Victor Glover is the first Black man in deep space.
Christina Koch is a NASA astronaut on Artemis II.
Christina Koch is the first woman in deep space.
Jeremy Hansen is a Canadian Space Agency astronaut on Artemis II.
Jeremy Hansen is the first non-American on a lunar mission.
Artemis II is a test flight to validate life support systems.
Artemis II carries humans approximately 252,000 miles from Earth.
Artemis II carries humans farther into space than ever before.
Artemis II will orbit the Moon but will not land.
A landing is planned for the subsequent Artemis III mission.
The Artemis II crew will perform a high Earth orbit before transferring to a lunar trajectory.
The Artemis II crew will loop around the far side of the Moon.
Artemis II will conclude with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
